description: The pure core module at packages/auth-service/src/core/index.ts:1 imports 'createHash' from 'node:crypto'. While SHA-256 hashing is deterministic given the same input, importing a Node.js built-in I/O module into what is declared as the 'Pure Core (deterministic, side-effect-free, formally verifiable)' module violates the stated purity boundary. The verification architecture (verification-architecture.md:13) explicitly states: 'No I/O. Fully unit-testable without mocks.' The node:crypto module is an I/O module that interacts with the operating system's cryptographic subsystem. The stateHash, oauthSessionHash, and linkSessionTokenHash functions depend on this import. While the output is deterministic for given input, the dependency on a platform-specific module compromises portability and formal verifiability claims. The purity boundary map in the behavioral spec lists these hash functions as pure, but their implementation relies on an OS-level crypto provider.
